frame_layout_resolved.method: every [ESP+k] in the 0x006a2e20 listing was resolved against the entry ESP, and the result was cross-checked against the two callees that consume the frame (0x00542b80 RET 0x4 and 0x006a2c50 RET 0x8). The chain is the fixating constraint: the epilogue's MOV ECX,dword ptr [ESP + 0x2c] must read the SEH record the prologue pushed, and only one entry-ESP alignment satisfies that together with ADD ESP,0x2c landing on the entry ESP.
frame_layout_resolved.insert_arm_entry_esp_note: the insert arm is reached only through the JZ at 0x006a2e77, which is after the found arm's PUSH ECX at 0x006a2e73; that pushed Property* is the source argument for BOTH 0x00542b80 calls, which is why the insert arm runs one dword lower than the found arm

frame_layout_resolved.cross_check_1: 0x006a2c50 reads its second stack argument into EBX with MOV EBX,dword ptr [ESP + 0xc] and then MOV EDX,dword ptr [EBX] to obtain the key. In the caller's frame that argument is entry_esp-0x24, and entry_esp-0x24 is exactly where 0x006a2e20 stored the property id. Key location confirmed from both sides.
frame_layout_resolved.cross_check_2: 0x006a2c50 reads its first stack argument with MOV ECX,dword ptr [ESP + 0x10] and writes MOV dword ptr [ECX],EAX then MOV byte ptr [ECX + 4],0x0 or 0x1. That argument is entry_esp-0x30, an 8-byte slot below the seed, so the out record cannot overlap the 0x18-byte seed.
frame_layout_resolved.cross_check_3: 0x00542b80 reads its source with MOV EDX,dword ptr [EBP + 0x8], which is the ESP value at its own CALL site. In the insert arm that is entry_esp-0x3c, and entry_esp-0x3c holds the Property* pushed once at 0x006a2e73 and shared by both arms. This is what fixes the insert arm's entry ESP.
frame_layout_resolved.conclusion: the seed Property begins at entry_esp-0x20, so its flags word is at entry_esp-0x10 and its type word at entry_esp-0x0e. The two zeroing stores and the post-insert bit test therefore all address the seed Property's own words, which is what the reconstruction models.

original_native_abi.return_semantics: void. The receiver is copied into EDI at 0x006a2e3b and is never moved back into EAX on any path; the epilogue restores the exception frame and returns. EAX is therefore scratch on every exit, and the only value the function produces is its effect on the receiver's map and its counter at +0x34.
original_native_abi.ghidra_prototype_caveat: Ghidra reports an unknown calling convention and a three-parameter (this, uint32_t, Property*) prototype. RET 0x8 admits exactly two stack arguments and ADD ESP,0x2c from the register pops lands exactly on the entry ESP, so the third declared parameter is a prototype artifact and no third stack slot is read. Ghidra's own decompilation also mislabels the two parameters, passing the id where the signature says Property* and vice versa.

in.name: App::DirectPropertyList::SetProperty
in.role: already reconstructed in pkg-direct-property-wave6; its base-set arm is this function

observed_mechanics: Installs a structured exception frame over the whole body, with filter 0x0120d6b8, before touching any list state, and restores it at the join.

Binary-searches the receiver's sorted property array for the property id through 0x00612db0, passing the map's begin (+0x18), end (+0x1c) and mode byte (+0x2c) plus the address of the id as the search key.

Treats the search as a hit only when the result is neither the end iterator nor greater than the id: CMP EAX,EBX rejects the end, and CMP EDX,[EAX] followed by the JB/JC at 0x006a2e64 (opcode 0x72) rejects an unsigned id below the found key. This is the canonical lower_bound-then-verify guard.
On a hit, assigns pValue straight into the entry's property at entry+4 with no insertion and no map mutation.

On a miss, builds a stack-local seed entry at entry_esp-0x24 holding the id, zeroes the seed property's flags and type words at entry_esp-0x10 and entry_esp-0x0e, assigns pValue into it, then hands the seed to the 0x006a2c50 find-or-insert so a new sorted slot is created by 0x006a2940.

After the find-or-insert, tests bit 0x0004 of the seed property's flags at entry_esp-0x10 and, when set, calls 0x0093db80 with the seed entry as receiver and argument 0. Because 0x00542b80 mirrors that bit in from the source, this is the read-only-source diagnostic, and because the argument is 0 the call is observationally inert.
Increments the receiver's operation counter at +0x34 exactly once per call, from both arms.
The 8-byte out record the find-or-insert helper writes at entry_esp-0x30 is discarded; the reconstruction models it as MapLookup and does not use it.
Returns void with the receiver untouched in EAX on every path.

unresolved_questions: The exception filter at 0x0120d6b8 and the exact cleanup handler 0x006a2e20 relies on were not identified; only the frame install and teardown are observed.

The map mode byte at receiver+0x2c is passed to 0x00612db0 and read by 0x006a2c50 at map+0x14, but the recovered 0x00612db0 overload does not vary its comparator on it, so what selects a different comparator is unresolved.
Semantics of the 8-byte {iterator, inserted} record are known but its value is discarded here, so no caller-visible use of it was found.
Behaviour of the slow assign path 0x00542c30 and of the unreconstructed callers 0x00bed460 and 0x00bed920 was not analysed.

The 4-byte slot at entry_esp-0x2c is written 0 before the 0x006a2c50 call and 0xffffffff after it, mirroring the SEH trylevel at entry_esp-0x04 from two frames away. It behaves like a compiler-kept active flag for the same __try scope, but nothing observable in this body reads it back, so its role is inferred rather than proven.

0x0093db80 is handed the seed entry at entry_esp-0x24 while that routine reads its receiver's words at +0x10 and +0x12, which inside a 0x18-byte entry address the Property's +0x0c and +0x0e words rather than its flags and type. With argument 0 the routine returns before using either, so nothing in this body distinguishes the two readings, but the receiver type does not match what the callee expects and the reason is not established.

The CONSTANTS WARN cannot be lifted by a reconstruction worker: the unparsed line is the toolchain listing grammar's missing JC synonym for JB, and that grammar lives in tools/**, which is out of scope. The instruction itself is reproduced in the source and its semantics are stated above.
